headline: Correction confirmed as AI unwind and a hawkish Fed collide
body: Friday's close pushed both the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory, more than 10% below their recent highs, after a seventh straight losing session, the longest skid since February 2020. The weekly damage was the sharpest in years: the Nasdaq's roughly 10% drop marks its worst week since 2020, with the S&P and Dow each down close to 8%. Selling was concentrated in the AI-infrastructure complex rather than spread evenly across the market, as semiconductor and data-center-adjacent names such as Micron, AMD and Broadcom each lost double-digit percentages in Friday's session alone, extending a pattern where the suppliers behind the AI buildout are absorbing the sharpest repricing.

Compounding the technical damage, Fed minutes released this week showed officials broadly airing concern about the risk of an AI-driven bust, a tone that cooled hopes for near-term rate relief and left prediction markets leaning toward a hike rather than a cut at the December meeting. Anthropic's IPO, priced at $83 and among the largest on record by proceeds, drew enormous demand but faded well off its opening pop, suggesting enthusiasm for one standout listing hasn't translated into broader conviction about the AI trade. Retail-sentiment chatter was again too thin and undated in today's search results to read with confidence, so this assessment leans on price action, Fed commentary and sector-level moves rather than confirmed social positioning.
